policy: Korean is canonical. Translations are display aids only. Never fabricate official English or Chinese names: a translation is shown only when its confidence is canonical/official/manual-derived/curated. Entries marked needs-verification or fallback are stored for review but render Korean. Visa/status codes (D-2, F-4, E-7, G-1, G-1-5, ...) are never translated.

basic_certificate.source: Widely used in Korean administrative/embassy/apostille contexts
basic_certificate.notes: The underlying statute (Act on Registration of Family Relations Art. 15(1)2, verified via law.go.kr/KLRI this session) literally translates this document type as 'Identification certificate'. Chose the practically-used 'Basic Certificate' instead because it is what applicants actually encounter on Korean administrative/embassy checklists; flagging the statute's literal wording here for transparency rather than silently picking one.

certificate_of_all_registered_matters.notes: The exact compound 'Certificate of All Registered Matters' is a reasonable construction from adjacent statute language ('all ... matters' + 'certificate of registered matters'), not a verbatim quoted phrase — hence manual-derived rather than official.
